- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mid-to-late horizon (days 10–20) when sentiment is mixed; apply a 1–3% downward bias to days 10–20 if sentiment is >0.5.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–2% for next 2–3 days if sentiment >0.75.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect potential rebound.
